fields.title: 📖 Justice does not mean elevating the Ḥarām
fields.body:
🖋️ **ʿAbdullāh b. Aḥmad** asked his father, **Imām Aḥmad**, about a Jewish man who claimed against a Muslim that he had poured out his wine.

> ***“There is no price for wine; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the price of wine.”***

Then Imām Aḥmad explained further: if the Muslim poured out the wine, he does not rule that he must replace anything for it. At the same time, Muslims are prevented from harming Ahl adh-Dhimmah or spoiling anything of theirs; if they destroy something of theirs that is not among what Allah has forbidden, they are liable for it.

🌙 **Conclusion:** Ahlus-Sunnah join **firmness in the Ḥarām** with **justice in dealings**. In the Islamic ruling, wine remains without a recognized price, but that permits neither arbitrariness nor unjust harm against people.

immutable.source: 📝 ʿAbdullāh b. Aḥmad, Masāʾil al-Imām Aḥmad riwāyat ibnuhu ʿAbdullāh, Bāb: idhā atlafa ʿalā dhimmī khamran aw ināʾa khamr, Nr. 1176, S. 317.
